Implementation Plan

Planning facts are confirmed: the read profile's `Read`/`Grep`/`Glob` have no path limits, the OAuth token sits in the CLI's own environment, and the container + relay pattern is already in the repo to reuse. I'm writing the plan.

Implementation plan — Issue: read-profile Claude roles can read credential files (finding `read-profile-can-access-credential-files`, Refs #3576)

Planning ref: `git rev-parse HEAD` = `78f8a7613109941c81cace29eb58b559a7669249`, branch `claude/replace-claude-sessions-phase-5d` (this is also the integration branch; no mismatch).

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends claude_run
Scope-mode justification: The answers set the scope. Q1=B puts the fix in the engine (`claude_run` in `scripts/ai_engine.sh` plus the read-profile settings in `scripts/claude_engine.py`), so it covers every read-profile Claude call: the `READ_ROLES` set and every caller that passes `AI_ENGINE_READ_ONLY=true` (SUMMARISER, BEHAVIOURAL_SMOKE, the read pass of RB_JUDGE). Write-profile roles are out of scope (Q1=C was not chosen). Q2=C makes filesystem isolation the main control and deny rules a second layer. The plan reuses the isolation the repo already has: the `--network none` / `--read-only` container from `scripts/clarify_isolated_run.sh` and `scripts/review_untrusted_sandbox.sh`, and the host-side token relay `scripts/claude_anthropic_relay.py`. With the relay, the real OAuth token never enters the container, so reading `/proc/*/environ` inside it finds only the placeholder. The only new code is the per-call snapshot builder and the container launch inside `claude_run`. A new standalone script or Dockerfile would have to be staged in a dozen workflows, so the Dockerfile text goes inline and the snapshot logic becomes a subcommand of `claude_engine.py`, which is already staged everywhere `ai_engine.sh` is. Per §6 (Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed), when isolation is unavailable the call falls back to the caller's existing codex/OpenCode path (exit 75). It never runs a read-profile Claude call on the host without isolation.

Automation / §20 section
- New script? No. The change extends `scripts/ai_engine.sh` (`claude_run`) and `scripts/claude_engine.py` (one new subcommand, one new `settings` flag). No standalone or manual script, no supervisor, no DB work, and no entry in `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`.
- Entry points: the existing call sites that already call `claude_run` / `claude_run_selected`. Support staging must also stage `claude_anthropic_relay.py` next to `ai_engine.sh` where it is missing today: `.github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml` (the `for f in … ai_engine.sh claude_engine.py codex_stall_guard.sh` loop, ~line 379) and `.github/workflows/workflow-failure-heal-intake.yml`. The implementer must check how that workflow stages `ai_engine.sh`. `review_autofix.yml` already has it through `OPTIONAL_BOOTSTRAP_SCRIPTS` in `scripts/stage_workflow_support.sh`. `security-audit.yml` sources it from `SECURITY_AUDIT_SUPPORT_DIR/scripts`, which is a full support checkout.
- Supervisor: none.

Conflicts and repo state the implementer must know
1. The working tree does not match the branch. `git status` shows ` M scripts/ai_engine.sh` and ` M scripts/claude_engine.py`. These are the support copies staged in-tree from `main` (the staged-support ledger behaviour described in agents.md). They lack `claude_run_selected`, `AI_ENGINE_READ_ONLY`, `READ_PROFILE_DENY` and the `read-guard` subcommand. This plan is based on the committed versions (`git show HEAD:scripts/ai_engine.sh` / `HEAD:scripts/claude_engine.py`). The implement run's staged-support restore handles this; the implementer must edit the HEAD versions.
2. The clarification options named CLARIFY and PLAN as read-profile roles. On HEAD, `READ_ROLES = ("CLARIFY", "CLARIFY_RESPOND", "SECURITY_JUDGE", "SECURITY_AUDIT", "WORKFLOW_HEAL")`, so PLAN uses the write profile and is not covered by Q1=B. CLARIFY and CLARIFY_RESPOND normally run inside `clarify_isolated_run.sh`'s own container, not through `claude_run`. They are covered by the new deny rules, and by the new isolated path if they ever reach `claude_run`.
3. The finding cites `scripts/summarize_reviewer_consensus.sh:371`. That call runs `claude_run_selected SUMMARISER … "${summariser_workspace}"` with `AI_ENGINE_READ_ONLY=true`, where `summariser_workspace` is `${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-$(pwd)}` (line 281). That checkout has `.git/config`, and possibly `.codex-workflow-src*/.git/config`, both carrying the `actions/checkout` auth `extraheader`. The token pool sits at `${RUNNER_TEMP}/claude-pool/tokens/*`. The read profile's `READ_PROFILE_ALLOW` gives unscoped `Read`, `Grep` and `Glob`. `claude_run` exports `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` into the CLI's own process, so `Read(/proc/self/environ)` also exposes it. The finding is confirmed.
4. Additional hole found: `Bash(git diff*)` is allowed in the read profile, and `git diff --no-index <any-host-file> /dev/null` reads any file on the host. The read-guard (`_READ_GUARD_GIT_OPTIONS`) does not block `--no-index`. This plan closes it.
5. Observed but out of scope: `clarify_isolated_run.sh` renders the read profile with `--guard-hook /guard.py`, but `cmd_settings` sets `read_guard_hook=str(Path(__file__).resolve())`, a host path that does not exist inside the clarify container. The new `--read-guard-hook` flag added here makes the fix easy, but clarify is not changed in this issue.

1. Files likely to change
- `scripts/ai_engine.sh` (HEAD version): `claude_run` sends `profile=read` to a new isolated path. Header comment updated.
- `scripts/claude_engine.py` (HEAD version): new `read-snapshot` subcommand, a `--read-guard-hook` option for `settings`, and more `READ_PROFILE_DENY` entries plus `--no-index` in the read-guard.
- `.github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml`: add `claude_anthropic_relay.py` to the staging loop. Check size with `wc -c`; this is a one-token addition.
- `.github/workflows/workflow-failure-heal-intake.yml`: stage `claude_anthropic_relay.py` next to `ai_engine.sh`, if that workflow stages its support files individually.
- `tests/test_ai_engine.py`: new isolated-path tests using stub `docker` and stub relay binaries on `PATH`.
- `tests/test_claude_engine.py`: tests for the snapshot, the deny list, `--read-guard-hook` and `--no-index`.
- `tests/test_claude_settings_policy.py`: extend if it pins the read-profile deny list.
- `agents.md`: one paragraph next to "Claude's read-profile Bash tool uses `scripts/claude_engine.py read-guard`…".
- `README.md`: rows for `CLAUDE_READ_SNAPSHOT_MAX_FILES` and `CLAUDE_READ_SNAPSHOT_MAX_BYTES`.
- `changelog.d/6262-read-profile-claude-isolation.md` (new). The issue number comes from the memory record; use the real issue number if it differs.

2. Functions / modules to implement

A. `scripts/claude_engine.py`
- `READ_PROFILE_DENY` gets these defence-in-depth entries. Each needs a `# <finding id>` comment, following the existing `#6217` style:
  `Read(//proc/**)`, `Grep(//proc/**)`, `Glob(//proc/**)`,
  `Read(**/.git/config)`, `Grep(**/.git/config)`, `Read(**/.git-credentials)`, `Read(**/.netrc)`,
  `Read(~/.config/gh/**)`, `Grep(~/.config/gh/**)`, `Read(~/.claude/.credentials.json)`,
  `Read(**/claude-pool/**)`, `Grep(**/claude-pool/**)`, `Glob(**/claude-pool/**)`,
  `Bash(git * --no-index*)`.
  Rule syntax: `//` means an absolute path, `~` means home, `**` is gitignore-style. This matches the template's `Edit(//__CHECKOUT__/…)` usage.
- `_READ_GUARD_GIT_OPTIONS` gets `"--no-index"`, so abbreviated and clustered forms are denied by the existing prefix matcher. `READ_GUARD_SAFE_EXACT` stays the same.
- `settings` gets an optional `--read-guard-hook PATH`, which must be absolute and is validated like the other paths in `render_settings`. Without it, the current value `Path(__file__).resolve()` is used, so existing callers behave the same.
- New subcommand `read-snapshot --source DIR --dest DIR [--git-objects-mount /git-objects] [--omit-claude-md]`, backed by a new `build_read_snapshot()`. It writes a JSON summary `{files, bytes, git}` to stdout. Behaviour:
  - File list: `git -C source ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard` when `source` is a git work tree; otherwise `os.walk` without following symlinks.
  - Excluded: any path part equal to `.git`, starting with `.codex-workflow-src`, `.env*`, `secrets` or `credentials`; basenames `.git-credentials` and `.netrc`; suffixes `.pem .key .p12 .pfx .keystore`; symlinks (skipped); files over 2 MiB (skipped); non-regular files. `CLAUDE.md` is left out when `--omit-claude-md` is passed, replacing the `mv` hide trick.
  - Copying follows `clarify_isolated_run.sh`: walk parents with `lstat`, open with `O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW`, compare dev/ino/size with `fstat`, write with `open("xb")`, mode 0644.
  - Totals are capped by `CLAUDE_READ_SNAPSHOT_MAX_FILES` (default `20000`) and `CLAUDE_READ_SNAPSHOT_MAX_BYTES` (default `268435456`). Over the cap, the subcommand exits non-zero with `read snapshot limit exceeded`.
  - Git metadata, only when the source is a repo whose objects directory (from `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`) has no `info/alternates`: `git init -q` in dest; write `.git/objects/info/alternates` = `/git-objects`; copy refs (`refs/heads`, `refs/remotes`, `refs/tags`) with `for-each-ref` piped into `update-ref --stdin`; set a detached `HEAD` to the source HEAD SHA; then `GIT_INDEX_FILE` + `read-tree HEAD`. The resulting `.git/config` is the default `git init` config: no remote, no `extraheader`, no `credential.*`, no `includeIf`. When the source has its own alternates or no HEAD, report `git: "absent"` and continue. In that case read-profile `git log/show/diff` inside the container fail, which is acceptable.
  - Every git subprocess runs with `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`, and `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null` for the dest repo, so host config does not leak into the snapshot.
